summary: Delivered the PH-281 read-only membership / project-scope / authorization-audit operations view. New `core/identity_read_services.py` exposes `member_access_snapshot` (members with masked display name, role, active/version, ProjectMember project-scope refs, derived AgentToken counts by state as of a date, last identity-audit change, pagination up to 200), `member_access_audit` (identity.membership.changed / agent_token.created / agent_token.revoked summaries with only safe payload keys, member filter and since/as_of bounds) and `member_access_issues` (inactive member holding an active token, expired-but-not-revoked token, company-scope role carrying project scope, cross-organization project scope, members with version changes missing identity audit, duplicate same-name active tokens). The page uses a new canonical `identity-access/` route declared in `pmo_plugins/delivery/domain_metadata.py` with access=history_read (delivery/urls.py imports it, no metadata copy), core/identity_views.py + identity_forms.py + core/templates/core/identity_access.html. Roles: owner/finance/auditor full; pm only managed-project member summary without other members' token lifecycle details; member denied; no token hash/auth snapshot/password/rate is exposed. The whole slice is read-only: no audit, receipt, session persistence, migration, canonical event or identity write; tests assert derived token/scope values, pm scoping, pagination/validation, permissions, module-disabled history readability, and zero INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE plus unchanged Membership/ProjectMember/AgentToken/AuditEvent/DomainEvent/Employee counts (append-only compatible). 14 scoped tests were added.

deviations: Post-review blocker fix (pm audit leak): member_access_audit restricted events only by organization/action when member_id was None, so pm could see other projects' identity.membership.changed / agent_token.* events. Fixed: when scope='project' the event stream is always restricted to visible member ids (entity_id, payload membership/target) and visible members' AgentToken entity ids, even without member_id; added a pm regression proving finance-project member identity/token audit is invisible to pm while owner sees it, and pm requesting that member still raises PermissionDenied. All other passing items were left unchanged.

Route wiring: the canonical `identity-access/` route was declared in `pmo_plugins/delivery/domain_metadata.py` (access=history_read) as authorized by the PH-298 planning slot; `pmo_plugins/delivery/urls.py` only imports and binds the handler, with no metadata copy.

AgentToken audit events (`agent_token.created/revoked`) are mapped to a member through the token rows because their AuditEvent entity is the token, not the membership; the audit summary still exposes only safe payload keys and never the token hash/auth snapshot.

`duplicate_active_binding` is only constructible in this BASE as duplicate same-name active tokens (org+user and project+member uniqueness are enforced by the schema), so that is the issue the service detects and documents.
The optional generic audit `core.identity_access.viewed` was not written: the Lead required zero audit for these read-only slices, so the page stays side-effect free.
pm sees a project-scoped summary only: project scope refs are filtered to managed projects and other members' token lifecycle/last-change fields are null.
